findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 25, Code C: 'Code C is used to report the partnership's adjusted basis in property other than money immediately before the property was distributed to you'. Code B: 'you may be required to recognize gain under section 737'.
findings.fix: Ask: 'Does box 19 show any code (A, B, C or another letter), even with a zero amount?' Add help saying that any code in box 19 counts, including property reported at zero basis.

findings.who: A partner who received marketable securities that are treated as money. The partnership reported them under code A at fair market value reduced by the section 731(c)(3)(B) reduction amount, which brought the figure to zero. The attached statement still shows the securities and their fair market value.
findings.why_no: Box 19 code A shows 0, so the filer answers that box 19 shows no amount. Any money distributed alongside the securities, or a later correction to the statement, never reaches the basis comparison.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 25, Code A: 'the partnership will use code A in box 19 to report its marketable securities at their FMVs on the date of distribution reduced (but not below zero) by the reduction amount'. The partnership 'will also attach a statement separately identifying' them.
findings.fix: Ask: 'Does box 19 show any code, or does an attached statement report a distribution to you?'

locators: p. 25, Box 19. Distributions, "Code A. Cash and marketable securities other than for services"

p. 25, Box 19. Distributions, "exceed the adjusted basis of your partnership interest immediately before the distribution, the excess is treated as gain from the sale or exchange of your partnership interest"

findings.who: A partner who is a real estate professional and materially participated in the partnership's rental real estate activity. Their K-1 shows a figure in box 2.
findings.why_no: The help quoted with the gate says box 2 is 'a passive activity amount for all partners.' A partner who knows their activity is nonpassive may decide the box-2 question does not apply to them and answer no, even though the box shows a number.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14, Box 2: 'the income (loss) in box 2 isn't from a passive activity if you were a real estate professional ... and you materially participated ... report box 2 income (loss) in column (i) or (k) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28.'
findings.fix: Keep the gate to the printed fact and change the help to say: 'Answer yes if any number other than zero is printed in box 2, whether income or a loss, and whether or not the activity is passive to you. Passive treatment is decided later.'

findings.who: A partner whose box 2 shows a loss printed in parentheses, such as (4,200), or with a minus sign.
findings.why_no: The gate's words 'show an amount' may be read as income only. A filer may not count a bracketed loss as an amount and answer no, which drops a loss the return should report or limit through Form 8582.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14, Box 2: 'If you have a loss from a passive activity in box 2 ... report the loss in column (g) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28' / 'follow the Instructions for Form 8582.'
findings.fix: Reword the gate as: 'Does box 2 show any amount other than zero, either income or a loss (a loss may be shown in parentheses or with a minus sign)?'

findings.who: A partner in a partnership with several rental real estate activities. The K-1 has an asterisk or a reference to an attached statement that lists the amount for each activity.
findings.why_no: The filer sees a statement reference instead of a single plain figure, or looks only at the statement. They may conclude that box 2 itself does not 'show an amount' and answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 14, Box 2: 'If the partnership had more than one rental real estate activity, it'll attach a statement identifying the income or loss from each activity.'
findings.fix: Add to the help: 'Answer yes if box 2 shows a total, or if the partnership's attached statement reports net rental real estate income or loss for box 2.'

locators: p. 14, Box 2. Net Rental Real Estate Income (Loss), "Generally, the income (loss) reported in box 2 is a passive activity amount for all partners"

findings.who: A partner whose Schedule K-1 box 20 has more codes than fit. The face of box 20 shows only an asterisk or "STMT" / "See attached statement". Code Z appears only on the continuation statement, which carries the 199A schedule showing QBI, W-2 wages, UBIA and possibly section 199A dividends.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether "box 20 show[s] code Z". The filer looks at the printed box 20, sees no letter Z there, and answers no without reading the attached box 20 continuation pages.
findings.line: k1p.box20z_if_any (QBI dropped to zero); k1p.z_other_if_z (section 199A dividends or cooperative refusal missed)
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 29, Code Z: "The partnership will provide the information you need to figure your deduction." p. 30: "Section 199A dividends. The amount reported reflects your distributive share of the partnership's net section 199A dividends."
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 20, or any statement attached for box 20 (it may show only an asterisk or 'STMT'), list code Z or a section 199A / QBI schedule?" Add help telling the filer to check the attached statements.

findings.who: A unitholder in a publicly traded partnership (or a large fund) who gets a substitute Schedule K-1 in the issuer's own layout. That K-1 reports section 199A information (qualified PTP income, QBI, section 199A dividends) on a separate supplemental schedule titled, for example, "Section 199A Information", without a recognizable "box 20, code Z" entry.
findings.why_no: The filer reads the question literally as "box 20 shows code Z". The substitute form has no such label, or uses its own line numbering, so the filer answers no even though the partnership furnished section 199A information.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 29, Code Z: "Generally, you may be allowed a deduction of up to 20% of your net qualified business income (QBI) plus 20% of your qualified REIT dividends, also known as section 199A dividends, and qualified PTP income from your partnership. The partnership will provide the information you need to figure your deduction."
findings.fix: Broaden the gate: "Does this K-1 (box 20 code Z, or any attached or supplemental statement) give section 199A, qualified business income (QBI), qualified PTP income, or section 199A dividend information?"

findings.who: A partner whose box 20 lists code Z with "STMT" in the amount column instead of a dollar figure, which is the usual way code Z is reported.
findings.why_no: The gated line is labeled "asked only when the box shows an amount (zero otherwise)". A filer who sees that label, or reads the gate with it in mind, may treat a code Z with no dollar amount as not counting and answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 29, Code Z: "The partnership will provide the information you need to figure your deduction."
findings.fix: Drop "when the box shows an amount" from the line label. Add help: "Code Z usually shows 'STMT' rather than an amount; answer yes if the code appears at all."

locators: p. 29, Code Z. Section 199A information, "The partnership will provide the information you need to figure your deduction"
p. 30, Section 199A dividends, "The amount reported reflects your distributive share of the partnership’s net section 199A dividends"

findings.who: A partner in a partnership with more than one non-real-estate rental activity. Box 3 on the K-1 shows an asterisk or "STMT", and the per-activity income or loss appears only on the attached statement.
findings.why_no: "Does box 3 ... show an amount?" They see no dollar figure printed in the box itself. They read "STMT" or the asterisk as "no amount".
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 14, Box 3: "If the partnership had more than one rental activity, it'll attach a statement identifying the income or loss from each activity." Also p. 14, Attached statements: "enter 'STMT' in the dollar amount entry space to indicate the information is provided on an attached statement."
findings.fix: On this Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), does box 3 (other net rental income or loss) show an amount, a loss in parentheses, or "STMT" or an asterisk referring to an attached statement? Count any of these as yes.

findings.who: A partner whose box 3 shows a loss printed in parentheses or with a minus sign, for example from equipment leasing.
findings.why_no: They may take "show an amount" to mean income. They may treat a loss, especially one they expect to be suspended under the passive rules, as "nothing to report".
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 14, Box 3: "If box 3 is a loss, follow the Instructions for Form 8582 to figure how much of the loss can be reported in column (g) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28."
findings.fix: Add to the help text: "Answer yes for income or a loss, even if you expect the loss to be limited. A loss is often shown in parentheses."

locators: p. 14, Box 3. Other Net Rental Income (Loss), "The amount in box 3 is a passive activity amount for all partners"

findings.who: A partner whose Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) has "STMT" or "See attached" in box 4a instead of a number. The amount of guaranteed payments for services is on a supplemental statement the partnership attached.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether box 4a "show[s] an amount." The box itself shows text, not a dollar figure, so the filer may answer no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 4a: "Guaranteed payments are payments made by a partnership to a partner that are determined without regard to the partnership's income. ... you should report them in column (k) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28"
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 4a show an amount, or refer to an attached statement (for example, 'STMT') that gives one?" Then ask for the amount from the box or the statement.

findings.who: A partner whose K-1 has an amount in box 4a, but who thinks of the payment as salary or a draw, or thinks it was for the use of capital rather than services.
findings.why_no: The parenthetical "(guaranteed payments for services)" may lead the filer to judge the nature of the payment instead of simply reading the box. They might say no if they believe the payment was not "for services."
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 4a: "Generally, amounts on this line aren't passive income, and you should report them in column (k) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28 (for example, guaranteed payments for personal services)."
findings.fix: Add help text: "Answer from what is printed in box 4a, whatever you call the payment (salary, draw, or other). The partnership's classification controls."

locators: p. 15, Box 4a. Guaranteed Payments for Services, "you should report them in column (k) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28"

findings.who: A partner whose Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), often a substitute form from a large or tiered partnership, shows only "STMT" or "See attached" in box 5. The interest amount appears only on the attached supplemental statement, for example because it is broken out by source or includes clean renewable energy bond credit interest.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether box 5 itself "show[s] an amount". The box holds a reference, not a number, so a literal reader answers no and never opens the statement.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 5: "Report interest income on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2b. If the amount of interest income included in box 5 includes interest from the credit for holders of clean renewable energy bonds, the partnership will attach a statement to Schedule K-1 showing your share"
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 5 (interest income) show an amount, or does it refer to an attached statement (for example 'STMT' or 'See attached')? If it refers to a statement, use the box 5 interest total from that statement."

findings.who: A partner whose K-1 is a substitute or software-generated form that does not follow the official box layout or numbering. Interest income appears under a label such as "Interest" or "Portfolio income – interest" rather than in a box numbered 5.
findings.why_no: The filer looks for a box numbered 5, does not find one with an amount, and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Portfolio Income: "Portfolio income or loss (shown in boxes 5 through 9b ...) ... Portfolio income includes income ... from interest"; Box 5: "Report interest income on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2b."
findings.fix: Add help text: "Box 5 is the interest income line. On a substitute K-1 it may be labeled 'Interest income' rather than numbered; answer yes if any interest income is shown on the K-1 or its statements."

locators: p. 15, Box 5. Interest Income, "Report interest income on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2b"

findings.who: A partner whose Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) prints "STMT", "See Statement" or an asterisk in box 6a. The dividend figure appears only on the attached supplemental statement, which partnerships often use when they report several activities or break out dividends.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether box 6a "show[s] an amount". The box itself shows a word or symbol, not a number, so a literal reader answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 6a: "Report ordinary dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3b." The same page also says: "The partnership attached a statement to the Schedule K-1 identifying the dividends included in box 6a or 6b"
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 6a (ordinary dividends) show an amount, or refer you to an attached statement (for example 'STMT' or '*') that gives one?" Help: "If the box points to a statement, answer yes and enter the total ordinary dividends from the statement."

findings.who: Same partner as above. The qualified-dividend figure is also given on the statement rather than in box 6b.
findings.why_no: The 6b line is reached only through the box 6a gate. A no caused by "STMT" in box 6a also drops the qualified dividends.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 6b: "Report any qualified dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a."
findings.fix: Same broadened gate as above. Add to the 6b question: "include qualified dividends shown on an attached statement."

findings.who: A partner whose K-1, through a partnership error, leaves box 6a blank but shows an amount in box 6b.
findings.why_no: Box 6a truthfully shows no amount, so the gate is no. The 6b amount is never asked, and nothing prompts the filer to get a corrected K-1.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 6b: "Report any qualified dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a."
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 6a or 6b show an amount?" If 6b exceeds 6a, flag the inconsistency (the help already says 6b is never more than 6a).

locators: p. 15, Box 6a. Ordinary Dividends, "Report ordinary dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3b"
p. 15, Box 6b. Qualified Dividends, "Report any qualified dividends on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 3a"

findings.who: A partner whose K-1 shows "STMT", "See attached" or an asterisk in box 8 instead of a number. The partnership reports the net short-term capital gain or loss on a supplemental statement, which is common for tiered or multi-activity partnerships.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether box 8 "show[s] an amount". The box itself shows no figure, only a reference to a statement, so the filer reads it literally and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 8: "Report the net short-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 5."
findings.fix: Ask: "Does box 8 (net short-term capital gain or loss) show an amount, or refer to an attached statement that reports one? Answer yes for a gain or a loss, including an amount in parentheses."

findings.who: A partner whose box 8 shows a loss printed in parentheses, such as (2,350), with no minus sign.
findings.why_no: The filer may read the parenthesized figure as not "an amount" or not a "gain", and answer no. The partnership's short-term loss is then dropped from Schedule D, line 5.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 8. Net Short-Term Capital Gain (Loss): "Report the net short-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 5."
findings.fix: Add help text: "A loss is often printed in parentheses; it is still an amount. Answer yes."

findings.who: Any partner who answers yes to the gate.
findings.why_no: No wrong no results. The gated line repeats the gate as a helper choice ("Box 8 shows an amount" true → line 8, false → zero). If the helper and the gate diverged, a yes could still yield zero.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 8: "Report the net short-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 5."
findings.fix: Bind the line's choice directly to the gate input k1p.has_b8, or drop the redundant helper and use k1p.box8 whenever the gate is yes.

locators: p. 15, Box 8. Net Short-Term Capital Gain (Loss), "Report the net short-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 5"

findings.who: A partner whose partnership had collectibles gain (for example, $500 from sold art or coins) offset by an equal other net long-term capital loss. Box 9a nets to zero and is left blank, but box 9b shows $500. The filer also has $10,000 of long-term gains from stock sales elsewhere on the return.
findings.why_no: Box 9a, net long-term capital gain (loss), shows no amount, so the filer truthfully answers no. The 9b/9c question is never reached.
findings.line: k1p.has_b9bc_if_9a (forced false), so the box 9b collectibles amount never reaches line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet and $500 is taxed at 15% instead of 28%
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 16, Box 9b: "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet—Line 18 in the Instructions for Schedule D (Form 1040)."
findings.fix: Do not nest the 9b/9c question under box 9a. Ask it on every Schedule K-1 (Form 1065): "Does box 9b (collectibles 28% gain or loss) or box 9c (unrecaptured section 1250 gain) show an amount or refer to an attached statement, even if box 9a is blank or zero?"

findings.who: A partner in a real estate partnership that sold depreciated buildings at a gain and investment property at a loss. The net long-term result is zero, so box 9a is blank, but box 9c shows unrecaptured section 1250 gain. The filer has other long-term gains on the return.
findings.why_no: Box 9a shows no amount. The help text "Both are parts of the gain in box 9a" reinforces the belief that 9b and 9c cannot matter without 9a.
findings.line: k1p.has_b9bc_if_9a (forced false), so the 25% unrecaptured section 1250 gain is omitted from the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 16, Box 9c: "Report unrecaptured section 1250 gain from the sale or exchange of the partnership's business assets on line 5."
findings.fix: Gate the 9b/9c question independently of 9a. Revise the help to: "These are usually parts of box 9a, but they can show amounts even when box 9a is blank or zero."

findings.who: A partner whose box 9a shows "STMT" or "See attached" instead of a figure, with the net long-term capital gain or loss given on a partnership statement. This is common for multi-activity or tiered partnerships.
findings.why_no: The question asks whether box 9a "show[s] an amount", and the box itself contains no dollar figure.
findings.line: k1p.box9a_if_any (zero instead of the net long-term capital gain or loss for Schedule D line 12)
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 15, Box 9a: "Report the net long-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 12."
findings.fix: "Does box 9a show an amount, or a code or note such as STMT referring to an attached statement that gives a net long-term capital gain or loss?" with help: "If the amount is on a statement, answer yes and enter the statement's figure."

findings.who: A partner in a fund-of-funds partnership that passes through unrecaptured section 1250 gain from a REIT or RIC. Per the instructions, the partnership reports this on an attached statement rather than as a dollar amount in box 9c.
findings.why_no: Asked whether box 9c "show[s] an amount", the filer sees only a statement reference in the box and answers no.
findings.line: k1p.has_b9bc_if_9a (false), so the REIT/RIC unrecaptured section 1250 gain for worksheet line 11 is omitted
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 (2025) p. 16: "If it reports the other two types of unrecaptured gain, it'll provide an attached statement that shows the amount for each type of unrecaptured section 1250 gain."
findings.fix: "Does box 9b or 9c show an amount, or does the partnership attach a statement reporting collectibles gain or any type of unrecaptured section 1250 gain?"

locators: p. 15, Box 9a. Net Long-Term Capital Gain (Loss), "Report the net long-term capital gain (loss) on Schedule D (Form 1040), line 12"
p. 16, Box 9b. Collectibles (28%) Gain (Loss), "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet"

findings.who: A partner whose partnership had collectibles gain or unrecaptured section 1250 gain that was fully offset by other long-term capital losses. For example, $10,000 of collectibles gain and a $10,000 long-term loss leave box 9a at 0 or blank, while box 9b shows $10,000 or box 9c shows unrecaptured gain.
findings.why_no: The parent gate asks only whether box 9a shows an amount. When the partnership's netting leaves box 9a at zero or blank, the gate is false, and the box 9b and 9c question is never reached.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 16, Box 9b: "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet"; Box 9c: "Report your share of this unrecaptured gain on the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet". Neither instruction is conditioned on box 9a.
findings.fix: Remove the box 9a dependency. Ask on every Schedule K-1 (Form 1065): "Does box 9b or box 9c show an amount or 'STMT' (even if box 9a is blank or zero)?"

findings.who: A partner whose partnership reports more than one type of unrecaptured section 1250 gain, for example from a REIT, a RIC or a lower-tier partnership interest. Box 9c then reads 'STMT' and the amounts are on an attached statement.
findings.why_no: The gate asks whether box 9b or 9c 'shows an amount'. 'STMT' is not a dollar amount, so the partner answers no. The help that says the STMT case is outside the tool's scope is attached only to the gated question, so it never appears and the tool never refuses.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 16, Box 9c: "If it reports the other two types of unrecaptured gain, it'll provide an attached statement that shows the amount for each type of unrecaptured section 1250 gain."
findings.fix: Word the gate as "Does box 9b or 9c show an amount, a loss, or 'STMT'?" Move the STMT-is-out-of-scope help onto the gate question itself.

findings.who: A partner whose box 9a shows a net long-term capital loss in parentheses, for example (15,000), while box 9b shows a $5,000 collectibles gain.
findings.why_no: If the box 9a condition is answered by the filer and not computed from an entered amount, the label 'net long-term capital gain (loss)' and 'shows an amount' may lead the filer to say no when the box holds a loss.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 16, Box 9b: "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet"
findings.fix: Compute the condition from the entered box 9a amount (nonzero, including negative values). If it is asked, say "any amount, including a loss shown in parentheses." This is better resolved by the first fix, which removes the dependency.

locators: p. 16, Box 9b. Collectibles (28%) Gain (Loss), "Report collectibles gain or loss on line 4 of the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet"
p. 16, Box 9c. Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain, "If the partnership reports only unrecaptured section 1250 gain from the sale or exchange of its business assets, it’ll enter a dollar amount in box 9c"

findings.who: A couple files jointly for 2025, and the K-1 belongs to one spouse. That spouse filed single or married filing separately for 2024, and that separate 2024 Form 8582 shows an unallowed loss from this partnership. The other spouse is answering the questions.
findings.why_no: The gate asks about a loss held back on 'your 2024 return' and points to 'your 2024 Form 8582'. The person answering filed no 2024 return with that loss and no Form 8582. Read literally, the answer is no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): 'Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582.'
findings.fix: Ask: 'Was a loss from this partnership held back (not deducted) because of the passive activity rules on a 2024 or earlier return filed by you or your spouse, jointly or separately?' Add help text: 'Look at Part VII, column (c), of the 2024 Form 8582 filed by whichever of you owns this interest, or at your joint one.'

findings.who: A filer had a passive loss from this partnership suspended in 2021. Their 2024 return left out Form 8582, either by mistake or because a preparer or software skipped it, so no 2024 Form 8582 lists the carryover.
findings.why_no: The help says 'A 2024 Form 8582 (Part VII, column (c)) lists such a loss.' The filer finds no 2024 Form 8582 and concludes there was no such loss. The suspended loss still carries forward by statute whether or not the form was filed.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): 'Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity.'
findings.fix: Make the form one source among several: 'Usually shown in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582. If you didn't file one, check earlier years' Forms 8582 or ask your preparer. The loss still carries forward.'

findings.who: In 2024 some of this partnership's loss was allowed, for example under the $25,000 rental allowance or against other passive income, and the rest was suspended. The filer saw a loss from the partnership on their 2024 Schedule E.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'held back (not deducted)' as asking whether the loss was disallowed outright. Because a loss from this partnership appeared and reduced their income, they answer no, missing the partially suspended remainder.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): 'Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582.'
findings.fix: Say: 'Was any part of a loss from this partnership held back (not deducted), even if the rest was deducted?'

findings.who: The partnership changed its name or EIN, merged into a successor, or was grouped with another activity on the filer's 2024 Form 8582. Part VII therefore lists the suspended loss under a different name or under the grouped activity.
findings.why_no: The question says 'a loss from this partnership'. The filer finds no line on the 2024 Form 8582 matching the name on this K-1 and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): 'Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity.'
findings.fix: Add help text: 'Include a loss listed under this partnership's former name, a predecessor partnership, or an activity you grouped it with.'

findings.who: A preparer or software prepared the filer's earlier returns. The filer knows a K-1 loss 'didn't count' but not why, and does not recognize 'passive activity rules'.
findings.why_no: The filer cannot classify the reason the loss was held back. They answer no because they don't think of it as a passive activity matter, or because they assume a basis or at-risk limit applied.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): 'You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582.'
findings.fix: Ask first about the fact the filer can check: 'Does any 2024 or earlier Form 8582 (yours or your spouse's) list this partnership in its unallowed-loss worksheet?' Treat 'not sure' as yes and follow with the box questions.

findings.who: A filer has a prior-year unallowed commercial revitalization deduction (CRD) from rental real estate held through this partnership.
findings.why_no: The gate asks about a held-back 'loss'. A filer carrying a CRD may not count a deduction as a loss and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Line 3: 'If you have prior-year unallowed commercial revitalization deductions (CRD) from rental real estate activities, treat that dollar amount as negative and combine with lines 1d and 2d.'
findings.fix: Add: 'Include a held-back commercial revitalization deduction (marked CRD on your Form 8582).' Alternatively, have the tool state that CRD is out of scope and refuse.

locators: p. 10, Part IV, "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582"

findings.who: A partner whose 2024 return was prepared by a paid preparer or software. The partnership's box 1 loss exceeded their passive income, so Form 8582 suspended part of it and listed the carryover in Part VII, column (c). The filer never saw this as a separate decision.
findings.why_no: "Held back" is a classification the filer must make without seeing it. They remember entering the K-1 loss and believe it was deducted, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Ask a fact the filer can check: "Did your 2024 return include Form 8582 (Passive Activity Loss Limitations)? If so, does Part VII, column (c) show an amount for this partnership?" Add help that this is common for losses from partnerships where the filer does not work.

findings.who: A partner whose 2024 Form 8582 allowed part of the partnership loss and suspended the rest, for example by netting it against other passive income or through the worksheets in Parts VII and VIII.
findings.why_no: Part of the loss did reduce their 2024 tax, so they read "a loss ... held back" as "was the loss denied" and answer no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Say "any part of a loss, even if the rest was allowed," and point to Part VII, column (c) of the 2024 Form 8582 as the test.

findings.who: A partner whose box 1 loss was suspended in 2019–2022 and carried through every later Form 8582. The 2025 K-1 shows income, or the 2024 K-1 showed income.
findings.why_no: They read "an earlier return" as last year's return, or tie "a loss from this partnership" to a recent K-1 loss. Last year's K-1 had no loss, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity."
findings.fix: Say "held back on any earlier year's return and not yet used, even if this year's or last year's K-1 shows income. Losses carry forward until used or the interest is disposed of."

findings.who: Spouses filing jointly for 2025. In 2024 the partner spouse filed separately, or filed before the marriage, and that separate Form 8582 suspended the partnership loss.
findings.why_no: The gate says "an earlier return" with no owner. The filer reads it as the couple's own earlier joint return, which does not exist, and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Say "held back on any earlier return of yours or your spouse's, including a separate or pre-marriage return."

findings.who: A partner whose interest continued after the partnership merged, converted, or changed its name or EIN. The 2024 Form 8582, Part VII lists the activity under the old partnership's name.
findings.why_no: "This partnership" doesn't match any name in their 2024 Part VII, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part V, Column (c): "Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity."
findings.fix: Add help: "Include losses listed under a former name of this partnership or a predecessor partnership whose business it continues."

locators: p. 10, Part IV, "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582"

findings.who: A couple filing jointly for 2025 who filed separate returns for 2024, or married in 2025. The spouse is the partner, and the spouse's own 2024 Form 8582 carried an unallowed box 2 rental real estate loss from this partnership. The other spouse is the one answering the tool.
findings.why_no: "A loss from this partnership held back on an earlier return" reads as the joint filer's own prior return. The prior joint return did not exist, or did not include the loss. The answering spouse never saw the spouse's separate 2024 Form 8582.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Ask: "Did you or your spouse have a loss from this partnership that wasn't allowed on a 2024 return, whether joint or separate? Check Part VII, column (c), of any 2024 Form 8582 either of you filed."

findings.who: A filer whose preparer or software labeled the amount "suspended passive loss", "passive activity loss carryover" or "unallowed loss". The 2024 Form 8582 Part VII, column (c), shows an amount for this partnership's rental real estate.
findings.why_no: The filer does not connect "held back" with "suspended", "carryover" or "unallowed". They may also read "held back" as the partnership withholding a distribution or tax, which did not happen.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Use the IRS term and point to the document: "Does your 2024 Form 8582, Part VII, column (c), show an unallowed (suspended or carryover) loss for this partnership?" Add help text: "This is sometimes called a suspended passive loss or a passive loss carryover."

findings.who: A filer whose rental real estate loss from this partnership was first disallowed in 2020 and carried forward each year since. It sits in Part VII, column (c), of the 2024 Form 8582.
findings.why_no: "Held back on an earlier return" can read as "last year's loss was limited". In 2024 the partnership's box 2 showed income or a fully allowed loss, so the filer thinks nothing was held back then. Yet the older carryover was still listed on the 2024 form.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582."
findings.fix: Say "from any earlier year, still not used as of your 2024 return". Prefer the document check: "Is this partnership listed with an amount in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582?"

findings.who: A filer whose 2024 Form 8582 lists this activity under a different name. The partnership may have renamed, merged into a successor, or been grouped with other activities as one activity.
findings.why_no: "From this partnership" leads the filer to look for this partnership's current name in the 2024 Part VII. The name is not there, so they answer no.
findings.irs_text: i8582 (2025) p. 10, Part IV, Column (c): "Enter the prior-year unallowed losses for each activity."
findings.fix: Add help text: "Include a loss listed under a former name, a predecessor partnership, or a grouped activity that includes this partnership's rental real estate."

locators: p. 10, Part IV, "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582"

findings.who: A limited partner whose box 3 rental loss was suspended on the 2024 return by the passive activity rules. Software or a paid preparer filled in Form 8582 automatically, so the filer never saw a loss 'held back'.
findings.why_no: The filer deducted what the software allowed and does not think of a passive suspension as a loss 'held back'. The IRS terms 'unallowed' and 'Form 8582, Part VII' do not appear in the gate, so the filer reads it as about something they chose to defer.
findings.irs_text: Column (c). Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582. (i8582 2025, p. 10, Part V)
findings.fix: Ask: 'Did your 2024 Form 8582 (passive activity loss limitations) list a prior-year unallowed or suspended loss for this partnership in Part VII, column (c)? If you used software or a preparer, check the 2024 Form 8582 or its carryover worksheet.' Explain that 'held back' includes losses the passive activity rules disallowed automatically.

findings.who: Spouses filing jointly in 2025 where the K-1 belongs to the spouse. The spouse's box 3 loss was suspended on the spouse's own 2024 return, filed single or married filing separately before the joint return.
findings.why_no: The filer completing the return reads 'held back on an earlier return' as their own or the couple's earlier joint return. Neither shows a suspended loss for this partnership, so the filer answers no.
findings.irs_text: Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582. (i8582 2025, p. 10, Part V)
findings.fix: Ask: 'Was a loss from this partnership held back (unallowed) on any earlier return filed by you or your spouse, including a separate or single return either of you filed?'

findings.who: A filer whose loss from this partnership was suspended in 2019 and carried forward unchanged on each later Form 8582. Nothing was 'held back' from the 2024 activity itself.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'held back on an earlier return' as last year's loss being limited. Their 2024 share showed income or no loss, so they answer no, even though the old suspended amount is still in 2024 Part VII, column (c).
findings.irs_text: Column (c). Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582. (i8582 2025, p. 10)
findings.fix: State that the gate covers a loss suspended in any earlier year and still carried forward, including one shown again on the 2024 Form 8582 although it arose years ago.

findings.who: A partner whose partnership merged, converted, or was restructured into the entity that issued this K-1. The 2024 Form 8582 lists the suspended loss under the predecessor's name, or under a grouped activity name.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'a loss from this partnership' as requiring the same name or EIN. The suspended loss appears under a different activity name, so the filer answers no.
findings.irs_text: Enter the unallowed losses for the prior years for each activity. You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582. (i8582 2025, p. 10)
findings.fix: Add help text: 'Include losses listed under a predecessor entity or a grouped activity that includes this partnership.'

locators: p. 10, Part IV, "You find these amounts in Part VII, column (c), of your 2024 Form 8582"

findings.who: A married filer on a joint return who did no work in the partnership in 2025, but whose spouse performed more than 500 hours in the partnership activity.
findings.why_no: The gate asks only whether 'you' worked in the business; the filer truthfully says no for themselves, not reading it as covering the spouse.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership ... is counted toward material participation'; test 1 is 'more than 500 hours during the tax year.'
findings.fix: Ask 'Did you or your spouse work in the business in 2025?' and count spouse hours in the gate; if either worked, ask the 500-hour question.

findings.who: A partner in a fiscal-year partnership whose more than 500 hours of participation fell during the partnership's tax year but outside calendar 2025, such as a tax year ending June 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate and gated question both say 'in 2025'; the filer truthfully had no or not more than 500 hours in calendar 2025, even though the partnership tax-year test is met.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'All determinations of material participation are based on your participation during the partnership's tax year'; test 1 is more than 500 hours during the tax year.
findings.fix: Use the partnership's tax-year dates, not '2025', in the gate and question.

findings.who: A partner with no box 1 ordinary business income or loss, or a zero box 1, but with separately stated deductions, credits, or prior-year unallowed losses from the partnership trade or business, who worked more than 500 hours in that activity.
findings.why_no: The tool computes the gate false solely because box 1 shows no amount, so it never asks about work and silently sets hours500 to zero.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Income (loss), deductions, and credits from an activity are nonpassive if you determine that you materially participated in a trade or business activity of the partnership.'
findings.fix: Gate on the existence of any activity item whose passive/nonpassive treatment depends on material participation, not only box 1; or ask material participation per activity.

findings.who: A real estate professional partner who worked more than 500 hours in a rental real estate activity held through the partnership; the K-1 shows rental real estate income or loss in box 2 and no box 1 ordinary business amount.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed only from box 1 and asks about 'the business'; a rental real estate activity is not reached, so the filer answers no or is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'if you were a real estate professional ... in each rental real estate activity held through the partnership' and material participation makes the activity nonpassive.
findings.fix: Include rental real estate activities in the gate and use 'activity' rather than 'business'; ask per activity.

findings.who: A partner in a multi-activity partnership who did not work in the activity that produced the box 1 amount but worked more than 500 hours in another trade or business activity identified on the attached statement.
findings.why_no: The gate asks singularly whether the filer 'worked in the business' on this K-1; the filer reads that as the activity shown by box 1 and says no, even though the 500-hour test is met for another activity.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'If the partnership had more than one activity, it'll attach a statement ... identifies each activity' and 'You must determine if you materially participated ... in each trade or business activity held through the partnership.'
findings.fix: Ask the work and 500-hour questions separately for each activity identified on the K-1 statement, not once for the K-1.

findings.who: A limited partner who performed more than 500 hours of work in the partnership activity but believes limited partners are merely investors and cannot 'work in the business.'
findings.why_no: The gate asks for a legal conclusion ('worked in the business') rather than the checkable fact ('participated in the activity'), so the limited partner answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Limited partners. If you're a limited partner, you must meet item 1, 5, or 6 above'; item 1 is 'more than 500 hours during the tax year.'
findings.fix: Ask whether the filer or spouse participated in the activity for more than 500 hours; separately state that limited partners can qualify under test 1.

findings.who: A partner who did more than 500 hours of unpaid work in the partnership activity but was not paid wages or guaranteed payments.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'worked in the business' as paid employment and says no because they received no compensation.
findings.irs_text: i1065sk1 p. 9: 'Generally, any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership ... is counted toward material participation.'
findings.fix: Say 'performed work or services, whether or not paid,' in the gate or help.

locators: p. 9, Individuals (other than limited partners), "You participated in the activity for more than 500 hours during the tax year"
p. 9, Work counted toward material participation, "any work that you or your spouse does in connection with an activity held through a partnership"
